content:
Another millennial nostalgia post. Get ready to snooze if you’re a Gen Z, get ready to reminisce if you’re a fellow millennial, and get ready to ponder if you’re a fellow deep thinker like me.

This is about one of the greatest anime shows ever (for me) – Dragonball Z. I used to watch this on TV when I was a kid (probably age 8-13), perfect match for a young and athletic boy who was also enrolled in Judo and Taekwondo since age 6. And back then, we didn’t have on-demand streaming or YouTube, so the only way to watch this was to “wait” for that 30 min time-slot on TV every week at 8 pm, and I had to finish all my homework before that if I wanted a chance to watch it. To top that, that was also prime time for Indian daily soaps, so I REALLY had to beg my parents and grandparents to let me and my brother watch that for 30 mins on the only TV we had in our small rental apartment.

It was the best of times!

What I am reminiscing though is some of the philosophy of DBZ, which has changed for me over time as I’ve grown from a delusionally optimistic young kid with boundless dreams, into a semi-jaded, semi-disillusioned man who is now finding and hitting every wall imaginable that stands between dreams and reality. And this whole contrast can be found by looking at the contrast between the characters of Goku and his arch-rival (and later arch-friend) Vegeta.

Inspiration for the child: Goku

The Dragonball manga was originally inspired by the 16th century Chinese classic novel Journey to the West. Son Goku = Sun Wukong. Very similar carefree, mischievous, audacious personality, combined with all-world strength and unshakeable righteousness. Just like Wukong, Goku was a God. The example of perfection, the ideal to strive for, the one to remember every time you were beaten down and wanted to hope. Just power up to Super Saiyan Level 2, and beat the shit out of your enemy. That’s how it was. And yes, the Frieza Saga to this day is the most epic Anime saga ever, maybe only matched by the Pain Saga in Naruto.

How was Goku not the most inspiring thing for a kid? Happy, strong, eat what you want, and in the end you always win.

Inspiration for the adult: Vegeta

As it happens, for the vast majority of kids (not born in privilege), you don’t always win, especially when you grow up and unlike the privileged you have to fight through all the “systems” designed to keep the lower and middle classes where they are (education, corporate jobs, immigration etc.). You come across a lot of walls, a LOT of walls. And if you’re ambitious, but not lucky, you’re in for a ride.

This is where recently I started remembering Vegeta’s story. Arrogant and ambitious to start off, selfish, greedy, cunning, unreliable, just like any human, and definitely not like the gods Goku or Wukong. He was inflicted by all the human seven deadly sins, but we kinda thought he was a villain. Now I realize that if he was a villain, then all of us are villains too.

Where his story hid me the hardest was his quest to become a super saiyan. That episode is one of the more spiritual lessons out there, where Vegeta describes his quest to become a super saiyan was fueled by the sole desire of being better than Goku and not staying in his shadow. He tried and tried, but couldn’t succeed, until he felt truly lost, gave up the desire and just let things be.

In real life, even this is not a guarantee that you’ll get what you want when you truly let go of the strings, but at least on the inside you feel at peace, and who knows maybe what you are searching for wasn’t able to come inside because you just didn’t have peace, and you were full of internal turmoil like Vegeta?

Well these were some of my thoughts and would love to hear if it resonates with anyone.

I leave you also with a relic from the early 2000s, the greatest AMV ever created, with the greatest song from Linkin Park, and on the greatest anti-villain in manga / anime history. Watch and cry.
